name: Bayesian Updating
description: Posterior inference via Bayes rule: combining prior beliefs with likelihood of observations. Foundational to Bayesian theories of perception and motor control. Neural implementation via population coding and probabilistic inference.
computational_signature: P(state | observation) = P(observation | state) * P(state) / P(observation)
key_references: Knill, D. C., & Pouget, A. (2004). The Bayesian brain: The role of uncertainty in neural coding and computation. Trends in Neuroscience, 27(12), 712-719.
Deneve, S. (2008). Bayesian spiking neurons I: Inference. Neural Computation, 20(1), 91-117.
empirical_evidence: Population decoding shows priors and posteriors consistent with Bayesian inference. Motion discrimination, depth perception, and reaching tasks all show Bayesian-optimal behavior. Uncertainty (posterior width) correlates with neural variability. Implementation via population codes and synaptic learning is plausible but exact circuit mechanisms unclear.
